title: Whose Head Was Nailed to Madurai's Gates? | Pandya Civil War, 1169 #shorts

lines.text: Whose head was nailed to the gates of Madurai?
Around eleven sixty nine, two Pandya princes fought for the throne of Madurai.
One of them, Parakrama Pandya, begged Lanka for help. Accounts say he was killed before it came.
lines.caps: *Parakrama | *Pandya | begged *Lanka | for help | accounts say | *killed | before it came

lines.text: The Lankan king Parakramabahu sent his general, Lankapura, across the sea.
Lanka's chronicle, the Culavamsa, says he won battle after battle, put the dead prince's son on the throne, and sailed home a hero.
lines.caps: the *Culavamsa | says he *won | battle after *battle | the son | on the *throne | home a *hero

lines.text: But Chola stone inscriptions tell a different ending.
They say king Rajadhiraja the Second sent an army, and the heads of Lankapura and another general were nailed to the gates of Madurai.
lines.caps: king *Rajadhiraja | *II | sent an *army | the *heads | of *Lankapura | *nailed | to the *gates

lines.text: Each side carved its own victory.
Historians still argue over the dates, and over whose record bent the truth.

lines.text: A hero's welcome, or a head on a gate? Tell me below. Then watch again, and see which story cracks first.
